## Phase 4: scripts

Create each shell script with `chmod +x`. They are bash, and they run on macOS's bash 3.2 as well as on Linux. The `.java` files are single-file programs the JDK runs from source (`java scripts/X.java`); they need the build JDK (25).

### 4.1 `scripts/bytecode-inputs.sh`: the compiled program and its classpath

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sourced by scripts/dead-code.sh and scripts/jdk-report.sh: the build's own compiled classes and the classpath they
# were compiled against, from Maven or Gradle. After `bytecode_inputs main` (or `test`):
#   PROGRAM    every module's class directories of that kind, absolute, one per line
#   LIBRARIES  every other entry of their classpaths, one per line (for `test`, the main class directories too)
#   RELEASE    the Java release the classes were compiled for (javac --release)
# proguard_classpath prints the classpath of the pinned ProGuard, resolved by the build tool (your mirrors apply).
# Paths must not contain spaces.
GATES_OUT=target/gates
if [[ ! -f pom.xml ]]; then GATES_OUT=build/gates; fi
mkdir -p "$GATES_OUT"
GATES_MEASURE=(-Dgates.werror=-Xlint:all -Dgates.nullaway=WARN -Dgates.errorprone.extra=-XepAllErrorsAsWarnings
  -Dcheckstyle.skip -Dcpd.skip -Dpmd.skip -Dspotbugs.skip -Dmdep.analyze.skip -Denforcer.skip)
JAVA_HOME_DIR="$(java -XshowSettings:properties -version 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^ *java\.home = //p')"

absolute_dirs() {  # the existing directories among $@, absolute, one per line
  local dir
  for dir in "$@"; do
    if [[ -d "$dir" ]]; then (cd "$dir" && pwd); fi
  done
}

bytecode_inputs() {
  local kind="$1" lists f
  if [[ -f pom.xml ]]; then
    local scope=compile output=classes
    if [[ "$kind" == test ]]; then scope=test; output=test-classes; fi
    # Compiled in measuring mode: this step needs the classes, not a verdict. The lifecycle gates are enforced by
    # `./mvnw verify` in scripts/validate.sh, and a baseline (Phase 6) must run before the code is clean.
    ./mvnw -q -B -ntp test-compile dependency:build-classpath -DincludeScope="$scope" "${GATES_MEASURE[@]}" \
      -Dmdep.outputFile="target/gates-$kind.classpath"
    lists="$(find . -path "*/target/gates-$kind.classpath" -not -path '*/node_modules/*' | sort)"
    PROGRAM="$(for f in $lists; do absolute_dirs "${f%/gates-$kind.classpath}/$output"; done)"
    MAIN_DIRS="$(for f in $lists; do absolute_dirs "${f%/gates-$kind.classpath}/classes"; done)"
  else
    ./gradlew -q gatesClasspath -Pgates.measure=true
    lists="$(find . -path "*/build/gates/$kind.classpath" -not -path '*/node_modules/*' | sort)"
    PROGRAM="$(for f in $lists; do absolute_dirs $(cat "${f%.classpath}.dirs"); done)"
    MAIN_DIRS="$(for f in $lists; do absolute_dirs $(cat "${f%/$kind.classpath}/main.dirs"); done)"
  fi
  LIBRARIES="$(
    {
      for f in $lists; do tr ':' '\n' < "$f"; echo; done
      if [[ "$kind" == test ]]; then printf '%s\n' "$MAIN_DIRS"; fi
    } | grep -v '^$' | sort -u | grep -vxF -f <(printf '%s\n' "$PROGRAM") \
      | while IFS= read -r entry; do if [[ -e "$entry" ]]; then echo "$entry"; fi; done || true
  )"
  local first
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  first="$(find $PROGRAM -name '*.class' -print -quit)"
  if [[ -z "$first" ]]; then echo "bytecode-inputs: no compiled $kind classes" >&2; return 2; fi
  RELEASE=$(( $(javap -v "$first" | sed -nE 's/.*major version: ([0-9]+).*/\1/p') - 44 ))
}

proguard_classpath() {
  local cp="$GATES_OUT/proguard.classpath"
  if [[ ! -s "$cp" ]]; then
    if [[ -f pom.xml ]]; then
      ./mvnw -q -B -ntp -f config/dead-code/proguard.pom.xml dependency:build-classpath -Dmdep.outputFile="$PWD/$cp"
    else
      ./gradlew -q gatesProguardClasspath "-Pgates.out=$PWD/$cp"
    fi
  fi
  cat "$cp"
}
```

### 4.2 `scripts/dead-code.sh`: dead Java code, two passes

ProGuard's shrinker is a reachability analysis: from the entry points it follows every call, field access, class reference, lambda and override, and `-printusage` lists what it never reached. No bytes are rewritten; nothing is written but the list. Tests sit in the same package as the code they test, so the test pass reads the production classes' package-private members too (`-dontskipnonpubliclibraryclassmembers`; without it ProGuard stops with "can't find referenced method"). Classes compiled from generated sources are kept whole. The scripts compile in measuring mode, so they run on a tree that has not reached zero yet (Phase 6); `validate.sh` has enforced the compile gates before it calls them.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dead Java code, two passes, one gate. ProGuard walks the program from its real entry points and lists every class,
# method and field it cannot reach.
#   --production  every module's main classes. Entry points: main methods, enum values()/valueOf(), serialization
#                 members, META-INF/services implementations and config/dead-code/keep.pro. Tests are not entry
#                 points: code that only a test calls is dead.
#   --tests       every module's test classes. Entry points: what JUnit and Mockito run or inject. A helper or fixture
#                 that no test reaches is dead.
# javac inlines compile-time constants (static final primitives and Strings), so their uses are invisible in bytecode:
# this gate never reports them, and Error Prone's UnusedVariable reports the private ones.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.."
# shellcheck source=scripts/bytecode-inputs.sh
source scripts/bytecode-inputs.sh
FOUND_EXIT=3

case "${1:-}" in
  --production) kind=main ;;
  --tests) kind=test ;;
  *) echo "usage: $0 --production | --tests" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

bytecode_inputs "$kind"
proguard="$(proguard_classpath)"
cp_args=()
if [[ -n "$LIBRARIES" ]]; then cp_args=(--class-path "$(paste -sd: - <<<"$LIBRARIES")"); fi

# JDK builds since 24 (Temurin among them) ship without jmods (JEP 493), which ProGuard usually reads the JDK from:
# extract the class files of the JDK modules the program and its libraries use, and of the modules those require
# (a supertype can live there), once per JDK and module set.
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
modules="$(jdeps --multi-release "$RELEASE" --ignore-missing-deps --print-module-deps --recursive ${cp_args[@]+"${cp_args[@]}"} $PROGRAM \
  | tr ',' '\n' | sort -u | paste -sd, -)"
while :; do
  required="$(for m in ${modules//,/ }; do echo "$m"; java --describe-module "$m" | sed -nE 's/^requires ([a-z0-9.]+).*/\1/p'; done \
    | sort -u | paste -sd, -)"
  if [[ "$required" == "$modules" ]]; then break; fi
  modules="$required"
done
jdk="$PWD/$GATES_OUT/jdk-$(java -version 2>&1 | head -1 | tr -dc '[:alnum:].')/${modules//,/_}"
if [[ ! -d "$jdk" ]]; then
  jimage extract --dir "$jdk" --include "regex:/(${modules//,/|})/.*" "$JAVA_HOME_DIR/lib/modules"
fi

services() {  # a keep rule for every implementation named in a META-INF/services file of this kind
  local source_sets=main source_set dir
  if [[ "$kind" == test ]]; then source_sets="test testFixtures"; fi
  for source_set in $source_sets; do
    find . -path "*/src/$source_set/resources/META-INF/services" -type d -not -path '*/node_modules/*' | while IFS= read -r dir; do
      sed -E 's/#.*//; s/[[:space:]]//g' "$dir"/* | grep -v '^$' | sed 's/.*/-keep class & { <init>(); }/' || true
    done
  done
}

generated() {  # a keep rule for every class compiled from generated sources (protobuf, Avro, OpenAPI...): not ours to trim
  local dirs="generated-sources" f pkg name
  if [[ "$kind" == test ]]; then dirs="generated-test-sources"; fi
  find . \( -path "*/target/$dirs/*" -o -path "*/build/generated/*" \) -name '*.java' -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
    | while IFS= read -r f; do
        if [[ "$kind" == main && "$f" == */build/generated/*/test/* ]]; then continue; fi
        pkg="$(awk '/^package /{ sub(/;.*/, "", $2); print $2; exit }' "$f")"
        name="$(basename "$f" .java)"
        printf -- '-keep class %s%s, %s%s$* { *; }\n' "${pkg:+$pkg.}" "$name" "${pkg:+$pkg.}" "$name"
      done
}

config="$GATES_OUT/dead-code-$kind.pro"
usage="$PWD/$GATES_OUT/unused-$kind.txt"
{
  printf '%s\n' -dontoptimize -dontobfuscate -dontpreverify -dontnote -dontskipnonpubliclibraryclassmembers \
    '-keepattributes *Annotation*,Signature,InnerClasses,EnclosingMethod,Record,PermittedSubclasses,NestHost,NestMembers' \
    "-printusage '$usage'"
  while IFS= read -r dir; do printf '%s\n' "-injars '$dir'(**.class)"; done <<<"$PROGRAM"
  while IFS= read -r lib; do
    if [[ -n "$lib" ]]; then printf '%s\n' "-libraryjars '$lib'(!module-info.class,!META-INF/versions/**)"; fi
  done <<<"$LIBRARIES"
  for module in ${modules//,/ }; do printf '%s\n' "-libraryjars '$jdk/$module'(**.class,!module-info.class)"; done
  if [[ "$kind" == main ]]; then
    cat <<'EOF'
# Entry points every JVM program has, and the members the JVM calls by name.
-keepclasseswithmembers class * { public static void main(java.lang.String[]); }
-keepclasseswithmembers class * { static void main(java.lang.String[]); }
-keepclasseswithmembers class * { <init>(); void main(java.lang.String[]); }
-keepclasseswithmembers class * { static void main(); }
-keepclasseswithmembers class * { <init>(); void main(); }
-keepclassmembers enum * { public static **[] values(); public static ** valueOf(java.lang.String); }
```

### 4.3 `scripts/TestReports.java`: every test class ran, and no test was skipped

Surefire only runs classes named `Test*`, `*Test`, `*Tests` or `*TestCase`, and a JUnit 4 test without the vintage engine never runs at all: both pass the build silently. A skipped test (`@Disabled`, a failed assumption, `@EnabledOnOs`) passes whatever the code does. This program reads every module's compiled test classes (with the JDK's class-file API) and JUnit XML reports, and fails on both.

```java
/*
 * Every test class ran, and no test was skipped. Reads each module's compiled test classes and the JUnit XML
 * reports Maven Surefire or Gradle wrote for them.
 *   never ran  a concrete class with JUnit test methods that no report mentions: a name the runner does not include,
 *              or a JUnit 4 test without the vintage engine.
 *   skipped    @Disabled, a failed assumption, @EnabledOnOs...: a skipped test passes whatever the code does.
 * Needs JDK 24+ (java.lang.classfile). Usage: java scripts/TestReports.java <repo dir>
 */
import java.io.IOException;
import java.lang.classfile.Annotation;
import java.lang.classfile.Attributes;
import java.lang.classfile.ClassFile;
import java.lang.classfile.ClassModel;
import java.lang.classfile.MethodModel;
import java.lang.reflect.AccessFlag;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.TreeSet;
import java.util.stream.Stream;
import javax.xml.XMLConstants;
import javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory;
import org.w3c.dom.Element;
import org.w3c.dom.NodeList;

final class TestReports {
  private static final Set<String> TEST_ANNOTATIONS = Set.of(
      "Lorg/junit/jupiter/api/Test;", "Lorg/junit/jupiter/params/ParameterizedTest;",
      "Lorg/junit/jupiter/api/RepeatedTest;", "Lorg/junit/jupiter/api/TestFactory;",
      "Lorg/junit/jupiter/api/TestTemplate;", "Lorg/junit/Test;");
  /** Where Maven and Gradle put compiled test classes, and where they write the XML reports of those classes. */
  private static final List<List<String>> LAYOUTS = List.of(
      List.of("target/test-classes", "target/surefire-reports"),
      List.of("build/classes/java/test", "build/test-results/test"));

  private final List<String> findings = new ArrayList<>();
  private int modules;
  private int testClasses;
  private int tests;

  public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
    Path root = Path.of(args.length > 0 ? args[0] : ".").toAbsolutePath().normalize();
    TestReports check = new TestReports();
    for (List<String> layout : LAYOUTS) {
      int depth = Path.of(layout.get(0)).getNameCount();
      for (Path classes : directoriesEndingWith(root, layout.get(0))) {
        Path module = classes;
        for (int i = 0; i < depth; i++) {
          module = module.getParent();
        }
        check.module(root, classes, module.resolve(layout.get(1)));
      }
    }
    System.out.printf("tests: %d modules, %d test classes, %d tests run%n", check.modules, check.testClasses, check.tests);
    check.findings.forEach(System.out::println);
    if (check.tests == 0) {
      System.out.println("tests: no test ran: run the tests first (./mvnw verify, ./gradlew check)");
    }
    System.exit(check.findings.isEmpty() && check.tests > 0 ? 0 : 1);
  }

  private void module(Path root, Path classes, Path reports) throws Exception {
    modules++;
    Set<String> ran = new HashSet<>();
    if (Files.isDirectory(reports)) {
      try (Stream<Path> files = Files.list(reports)) {
        for (Path report : files.filter(p -> p.getFileName().toString().matches("TEST-.*\\.xml")).sorted().toList()) {
          read(report, ran);
        }
      }
    }
    for (String testClass : testClassesIn(classes)) {
      testClasses++;
      if (!ran.contains(testClass)) {
        findings.add("never ran: " + testClass + " (" + root.relativize(classes) + "): Surefire runs Test*, *Test, *Tests"
            + " and *TestCase classes, and JUnit 4 tests need the vintage engine");
      }
    }
  }

  private void read(Path report, Set<String> ran) throws Exception {
    DocumentBuilderFactory factory = DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance();
    factory.setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true);
    factory.setFeature(XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, true);
    NodeList cases = factory.newDocumentBuilder().parse(report.toFile()).getElementsByTagName("testcase");
    for (int i = 0; i < cases.getLength(); i++) {
      Element testCase = (Element) cases.item(i);
      String className = testCase.getAttribute("classname");
      ran.add(className);
      tests++;
      NodeList skipped = testCase.getElementsByTagName("skipped");
      if (skipped.getLength() > 0) {
        String message = ((Element) skipped.item(0)).getAttribute("message");
        findings.add("skipped: " + className + "." + testCase.getAttribute("name") + (message.isEmpty() ? "" : " (" + message + ")"));
      }
    }
  }

  private static Set<String> testClassesIn(Path classes) throws IOException {
    Set<String> found = new TreeSet<>();
    try (Stream<Path> files = Files.walk(classes)) {
      for (Path file : files.filter(p -> p.toString().endsWith(".class")).toList()) {
        ClassModel model = ClassFile.of().parse(Files.readAllBytes(file));
        boolean concrete = !model.flags().has(AccessFlag.ABSTRACT) && !model.flags().has(AccessFlag.INTERFACE);
        if (concrete && model.methods().stream().anyMatch(TestReports::isTest)) {
          found.add(model.thisClass().asInternalName().replace('/', '.'));
        }
      }
    }
    return found;
  }

  private static boolean isTest(MethodModel method) {
    return method.findAttribute(Attributes.runtimeVisibleAnnotations()).stream()
        .flatMap(attribute -> attribute.annotations().stream())
        .map(Annotation::className)
        .anyMatch(name -> TEST_ANNOTATIONS.contains(name.stringValue()));
  }

  private static List<Path> directoriesEndingWith(Path root, String suffix) throws IOException {
    Path end = Path.of(suffix);
    try (Stream<Path> paths = Files.walk(root, 8)) {
      return paths.filter(Files::isDirectory)
          .filter(p -> p.endsWith(end))
          .filter(p -> !p.toString().contains("node_modules"))
          .sorted()
          .toList();
    }
  }
}
```

### 4.4 `scripts/mutation-report.sh`: the change's lines, mutated against their tests

PIT mutates the bytecode of every production class the change touched and runs the tests that cover each mutant. The report lists the mutants that no test killed (`SURVIVED`) or that no test reached (`NO_COVERAGE`), on the lines the change added or changed. A class whose test alone changed is reported whole: a test change is the moment to ask what else the tests miss. It builds with `package` (tests skipped) before PIT, so a module's shared test jar is the filtered jar of Phase 3.5 and not its whole `test-classes`, and in measuring mode, so it runs on a tree that has not reached zero.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The mutation report of a change: PIT mutates every production class the change touched; this lists the mutants
# no test killed (SURVIVED) or reached (NO_COVERAGE), on the lines the change added or changed (a class whose test
# alone changed is listed whole). A report you act on before merging or releasing, not a gate.
#   scripts/mutation-report.sh <base-ref>            # e.g. origin/main, or the last release tag
#   scripts/mutation-report.sh <base-ref> --whole    # every changed class whole
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.."
BASE="${1:?usage: $0 <base-ref> [--whole]}"
WHOLE="${2:-}"

changed_sources() {  # production sources the change touched, directly or through their test (FooTest -> Foo)
  git diff --name-only "$BASE" -- '*.java' | while IFS= read -r f; do
    case "$f" in
      src/main/java/*|*/src/main/java/*) if [[ -f "$f" ]]; then echo "$f"; fi ;;
      src/test/java/*|*/src/test/java/*)
        main="$(sed -E 's#src/test/java/#src/main/java/#; s#Tests?\.java$#.java#' <<<"$f")"
        if [[ -f "$main" ]]; then echo "$main"; fi ;;
    esac
  done | sort -u
}
class_of() { sed -E 's#^(.*/)?src/main/java/##; s#\.java$##; s#/#.#g' <<<"$1"; }
module_of() { local m="${1%%src/main/java/*}"; m="${m%/}"; echo "${m:-.}"; }

sources="$(changed_sources)"
if [[ -z "$sources" ]]; then echo "No production class changed since $BASE"; exit 0; fi
targets="$(for f in $sources; do class_of "$f"; done | paste -sd, -)"

if [[ -f pom.xml ]]; then
  out=target/gates
  # A report, not a gate: the other gates are skipped here so it also runs on a tree that has not reached zero.
  pit=(./mvnw -B -ntp package -Dmaven.test.skip.exec=true org.pitest:pitest-maven:mutationCoverage "-DtargetClasses=$targets"
    -Dgates.werror=-Xlint:all -Dgates.nullaway=WARN -Dgates.errorprone.extra=-XepAllErrorsAsWarnings
    -Dcheckstyle.skip -Dcpd.skip -Dpmd.skip -Dspotbugs.skip -Dmdep.analyze.skip -Denforcer.skip)
else
  out=build/gates
  pit=(./gradlew pitest "-Pgates.targetClasses=$targets" -Pgates.measure=true)
fi
echo "==> PIT on $targets (its log: $out/pit.log)"
mkdir -p "$out"
if ! "${pit[@]}" > "$out/pit.log" 2>&1; then
  tail -40 "$out/pit.log"
  echo "PIT failed: the tests must pass unmutated first" >&2
  exit 1
fi

for f in $sources; do
  cls="$(class_of "$f")"
  module="$(module_of "$f")"
  report=""
  for candidate in "$module/target/pit-reports/mutations.xml" "$module/build/reports/pitest/mutations.xml"; do
    if [[ -f "$candidate" ]]; then report="$candidate"; fi
  done
  if [[ -z "$report" ]]; then echo "--- $cls: no PIT report in $module (are its tests in $module?)"; continue; fi
  ranges=""
  if [[ "$WHOLE" != "--whole" ]] && ! git diff --quiet "$BASE" -- "$f"; then
    ranges="$(git diff --unified=0 "$BASE" -- "$f" | sed -nE 's/^@@ -[0-9,]+ \+([0-9]+)(,([0-9]+))? @@.*/\1 \3/p' \
      | awk '{ n = ($2 == "" ? 1 : $2); if (n > 0) printf "%d-%d ", $1, $1 + n - 1 }')"
    if [[ -z "$ranges" ]]; then echo "--- $cls: only deletions"; continue; fi
  fi
  echo "--- $cls (${ranges:-whole})"
  { grep -E "status='(SURVIVED|NO_COVERAGE)'" "$report" || true; } \
    | { grep -E '<mutatedClass>'"${cls//./\\.}"'(\$[^<]*)?</mutatedClass>' || true; } \
    | sed -E "s#.*status='([A-Z_]+)'.*<mutatedMethod>([^<]*)</mutatedMethod>.*<lineNumber>([0-9]+)</lineNumber>.*<description>([^<]*)</description>.*#\3 \1 \2: \4#" \
    | awk -v ranges="$ranges" '{
        keep = (ranges == ""); n = split(ranges, r, " ")
        for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) { split(r[i], b, "-"); if ($1 >= b[1] && $1 <= b[2]) keep = 1 }
        if (keep) print "    line " $0
      }'
done
```

Every mutant the report prints gets exactly one outcome before merge or release:
- a test that kills it;
- deleting the statement it proves has no effect;
- for an equivalent mutant (no test could ever tell it apart), the `@DoNotMutate` annotation below on the smallest method that holds it, with the reason. PIT skips any method or class that carries an annotation with that simple name.

`src/main/java/<ROOT_PKG as a path>/DoNotMutate.java` (create it the first time you need it, not before):

```java
package <ROOT_PKG>;

import java.lang.annotation.ElementType;
import java.lang.annotation.Retention;
import java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy;
import java.lang.annotation.Target;

/** PIT does not mutate what carries this annotation. Only for an equivalent mutant: say which, and why no test can see it. */
@Retention(RetentionPolicy.CLASS)
@Target({ElementType.METHOD, ElementType.CONSTRUCTOR, ElementType.TYPE})
public @interface DoNotMutate {
  /** The mutant, and why it is equivalent. */
  String value();
}
```

Do not run git commands that change the working tree (checkout, stash, commit) while PIT runs: it reads the compiled classes the build just wrote.

### 4.5 `scripts/validate.sh`: every gate, in order, each a hard stop

CI runs this script and nothing else.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Every gate, cheapest first; a green run here is a green CI run.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.."
# One command per step: under `set -e` a failure on the left of `&&` does not stop the script.
step() { printf '\n==> %s\n' "$1"; }

if [[ -f pom.xml ]]; then
  step "maven: enforcer, checkstyle, cpd, javac + error prone + nullaway, pmd, spotbugs, dependencies, tests"
  ./mvnw -B -ntp clean verify
else
  step "gradle: checkstyle, cpd, javac + error prone + nullaway, pmd, spotbugs, dependencies, tests"
  ./gradlew --no-configuration-cache clean check buildHealth
fi
step "every test class ran and none was skipped";  java scripts/TestReports.java .
step "the test JVMs' garbage collection";          java scripts/JfrGate.java --max-pause-ms 200 .
step "dead code: production";                      bash scripts/dead-code.sh --production
step "dead code: tests";                           bash scripts/dead-code.sh --tests

printf '\nvalidate: every gate passed\n'
```

Never add `-q` to the Maven step: quiet mode hides the compiler's and the dependency analysis' warnings, so a failure would print only "warnings found and -Werror specified".


---

## Phase 5: prove every gate works (mandatory)

On an existing codebase the gates already fail on today's findings, so a failure proves nothing about a plant. Add a scratch module first (a parent-inheriting `<module>` with one small class and its test, and `aspectjrt` if the repo weaves), prove that `./mvnw verify -pl <scratch-module>` is green with every gate enforcing, commit it in the scratch clone (the mutation row diffs against `HEAD`), and plant there. The CPD rows run from the root, and pass when the report names the scratch file. Delete the module when the table is done.

For each row: make the planted change in a scratch file (or a real file), run the gate, confirm it **fails with the message shown**, then revert it by deleting the scratch file or undoing exactly the lines you added. Put the table, with a ✔ per row, in your report. A row you cannot make fail means that gate is not wired: fix the wiring, not the row.

- `./mvnw -B -ntp verify` (**[gradle]** `./gradlew check buildHealth --continue`) runs every lifecycle gate; the script rows name their script. In a multi-module Maven build, run the lifecycle through `verify` (or at least `test-compile`), not `validate` alone: the enforcer resolves each module's dependencies, and a sibling module exists only once the reactor has built it.
- **javac's own warnings stop the compile before Error Prone looks**, so plant the javac rows and the Error Prone rows in separate runs.
- The messages are Maven's. Gradle prints the javac rows with their lint key (`warning: [cast] redundant cast to String`), CPD as `Found a 22 line (111 tokens) duplication in the following files:`, SpotBugs as `H P Dm: … forces garbage collection…`, and the dependency analysis as `Unused dependencies which should be removed:`.
- **[gradle]** Gradle runs every class with JUnit test methods whatever its name, so the "never ran" row needs a JUnit 4 test without the vintage engine there; the version-conflict row is `implementation` of an older version of a library another dependency brings (`Conflict found for module …: between versions …`).

1. **Dead code, imports, dependencies and duplication**: the two dead-code passes, Error Prone `Unused*`, PMD `Unused*`, Checkstyle imports, dependency analysis, CPD. Delete what is dead. For what is really used but invisible to the tool (a framework entry point, a class named in a config file), add a keep rule with a comment naming its caller. Extract duplicates into a class with a specific name, never `Utils` or `Helper`. Put shared test data in fixtures under `src/test`.
2. **Logic that says more than it does**: javac lint, Error Prone `Unnecessary*`, `Redundant*`, `ModifiedButNotUsed`, `PatternMatchingInstanceof`, PMD `Simplify*`, `Unnecessary*`, `Useless*`, SpotBugs `RCN_*`, `UC_*`, `DLS_*`. Error Prone fixes much of it itself; review every change it makes:

   ```bash
   ./mvnw -B -ntp clean test-compile -Dgates.werror=-Xlint:all -Dgates.nullaway=WARN -Dcheckstyle.skip -Dcpd.skip -Denforcer.skip \
     "-Dgates.errorprone.extra=-XepPatchChecks:UnusedVariable,UnnecessaryParentheses,MissingOverride,UnnecessaryLambda,UnnecessaryMethodReference,PatternMatchingInstanceof,UnnecessaryBoxedVariable -XepPatchLocation:IN_PLACE"
   ```

   Error Prone rewrites the files in place and does not format what it writes ("Refactoring changes were successfully applied"): run the repo's formatter on the changed files, review the diff, and compile again.
3. **Errors that disappear, resources and concurrency**: the catch and throw rules, `CloseResource`, `MustBeClosedChecker`, `StreamResourceLeak`, `FutureReturnValueIgnored`, `InterruptedExceptionSwallowed`, SpotBugs' multithreading patterns.
4. **Tests that test**: PMD `UnitTest*`, Error Prone's test checks, `TestReports` (a class that never ran, a skipped test), `CheckReturnValue` on AssertJ.
5. **Types that do not lie**: NullAway, then `-Xlint:rawtypes,unchecked`, then `CheckOptionalEmptiness`. This is the largest group. If it has more than about 150 findings, split the tree into packages that do not overlap and give each worker the "how to fix" rules below; a package nobody has reached yet gets `@NullUnmarked` in its `package-info.java`, and that list only shrinks.
6. **Memory**: `UnboundedStaticCollection`, `ThreadLocalWithoutRemove`, `ClassCanBeStatic`, SpotBugs `MS_*`, `NoThreadLeaks`; then size the test JVM (Phase 3.1), write collectability tests for the objects that register themselves and allocation budgets for the hot paths (Phase 0), and run `JfrGate`.
7. **Mutation on the change**: run `scripts/mutation-report.sh <base>` on the branch. Kill, delete or mark every survivor.

### How to fix each kind (the rules that keep the fix from becoming new slop)

- **`map.get(k)` or another `@Nullable` read**: prefer a shape that cannot be `null`:
  - `getOrDefault(k, fallback)` or `computeIfAbsent(k, …)` when the fallback is what the code *should* do;
  - iterate `entrySet()` instead of looking keys up;
  - an `EnumMap` or a record instead of a map used as a struct.

  If absence is impossible and nothing sensible can replace the value, throw a small named exception (`throw new UnknownSkuException(sku)`). Never `requireNonNull` a value just to quiet NullAway, and never cast.
- **The same read in a test**: `Objects.requireNonNull(prices.get("apple"), "the fixture prices apple")` names the fixture when it is wrong, or assert the whole structure (`assertThat(prices).containsExactlyInAnyOrderEntriesOf(…)`).
- **A null check or guard the types say can never fire** (SpotBugs `RCN_*`, Error Prone `ImpossibleNullComparison`), first decide where the value comes from:
  - **It crosses a boundary** (a request body, JSON bound by Jackson, a system property, an environment variable, a column, a library without nullness annotations): keep the guard and make the type honest: `@Nullable` on the field or parameter.
  - **It is internal and already has that type**: delete the guard.
  - **Check the producer before deciding.** If a shared type lies, fix it at its source and list any you leave.
- **An ignored `Future`**: `join()` it when order matters; return it to a caller that does; or hand it to an owner that joins or cancels it on shutdown. A future whose failure nobody observes is a swallowed exception.
- **A resource** (`CloseResource`, `StreamResourceLeak`, `OBL_*`): try-with-resources, including the streams of `Files.lines`, `Files.list` and `Files.walk`.
- **A thread or executor** (`NoThreadLeaks`): the object that starts it owns it and shuts it down; `try (var executor = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) { … }` for work that ends with the block.
- **A static collection** (`UnboundedStaticCollection`): a bounded cache (a `LinkedHashMap` with `removeEldestEntry`, or the repo's cache library with a maximum size), an instance field of an object with a lifecycle, or an immutable `Map.copyOf(…)` built once.
- **A `ThreadLocal`** (`ThreadLocalWithoutRemove`, `ThreadLocalUsage`): `static final`, and `remove()` in a `finally` around the work that set it; for request context, a `ScopedValue` (final since JDK 25).
- **An inner class that holds its outer instance** (`ClassCanBeStatic`): make it `static`. Since JDK 18 javac drops an outer reference the inner class never uses, which is why SpotBugs' `SIC_*` no longer fires on it; an anonymous class, a double-brace initialiser or a lambda that does use `this`, registered somewhere long-lived, still keeps the whole outer object alive.
- **An allocation budget exceeded**: find the site (`jfr view allocation-by-site`), then remove the allocation: a primitive instead of a wrapper, a loop instead of a stream on a hot path, a precompiled `Pattern` in a `static final`, no varargs or `String.format` per call. Never raise the budget.
- **Broad or empty `catch`**: catch the exception you can handle; otherwise let it propagate. Rethrow with the cause (`new FooException("…", e)`), and restore the interrupt flag (`Thread.currentThread().interrupt()`) when you catch `InterruptedException` and cannot rethrow it.
- **A cleanup that fails after the real failure** (a `finally`, or a catch that deletes a record, releases a lock, rolls back): the first exception is what the caller needs. Throw the cleanup's exception with the first one attached (`cleanupFailure.addSuppressed(original)`), or throw the original with the cleanup's attached; never let the cleanup's exception replace it with no trace.
- **A wrapper that hides what it wraps**: `catch (Throwable e) { throw new ConfigurationException("failed: " + e.getMessage()); }` drops the stack and names the wrong cause. Keep the cause, and pick the exception type from what failed, not from where it was caught.
- **A silent fallback on bad configuration** (an unknown algorithm name that falls back to MD5, a dimension that fails validation and is dropped): that is an error that disappears at the moment it is cheapest to see. Fail at configuration time with a named exception. Changing this changes behaviour (rule 5): report it with the fix, do not apply it.
- **A method only tests call** (a package-private `setClock`, `setHttpClient`, `resetForTests`): the gate reports it as dead, correctly. Give the production code the seam instead (a constructor or builder parameter that production passes too), and let the test use that. Do not add a keep rule for it.
- **An SPI method nothing calls** (an abstract method every implementation overrides and no caller invokes): delete it from the interface and every implementation, or report it if the interface is published API (removing it breaks callers outside the repo).
- **Shared mutable state** (Phase 2.10): `@Immutable`, a concurrent type, or `@GuardedBy` fields with the lock held on every access. A `LinkedHashMap` in access order changes on `get`, so a read needs the lock too.
- **A dead parameter** (`UnusedFormalParameter`): remove it from the signature and every caller. If an interface or framework requires it, that override is not reported.
- **Complexity over 12 or a method over 60 lines**: extract a well-named private method or a small class. Do not raise the limit.
- **A test the rules flag**: fix the test's shape (split it at four assertions, put a helper's assertion in a method named `assert…`). Never delete an assertion to pass a rule: move it into its own test. A skipped test is fixed or deleted with its reason in the commit, never left skipped.

## Phase 7: keep it (every future change)

- Run `scripts/validate.sh` before calling any change done. Green means every gate, not "mostly".
- Before merging or releasing, run `scripts/mutation-report.sh <base-ref>` and resolve every survivor it names (kill, delete, or mark as equivalent with `@DoNotMutate` and a reason). Write the survivor count and what you did about each into the PR or release notes.
- Adding code:
  - Make public only what another package uses.
  - A method or class only a test uses is dead.
  - Every object that registers itself somewhere gets a collectability test; every hot path gets an allocation budget.
  - An executor, thread, stream or connection has one owner that closes it.
  - An object more than one thread reaches is `@Immutable`, concurrent, or `@GuardedBy` (Phase 2.10).
  - A module that sets its own test `<argLine>` starts it with `${gates.test.argLine}`.
  - A catch that throws keeps the cause; a cleanup that fails keeps the first exception (`addSuppressed`).
  - No new `CPD-OFF` without its reason, no new keep rule or allowlist entry without its comment.
- Never raise a limit (complexity 12, nesting, 60-line methods, 500- and 900-line files, 4 assertions per test, 50-token clones, the test heap, an allocation budget, the pause bound). If something cannot fit, split it.
- Before a JDK upgrade, run `scripts/jdk-report.sh`. A production JDK upgrade changes `java.release` (**[gradle]** `gates.javaRelease`); a build JDK upgrade changes `requireJavaVersion` (**[gradle]** the `check` in the convention plugin) only once Error Prone supports that JDK. Re-measure the test JVM (Phase 3.1) after either.
- A finding that looks wrong is usually a type that lies, a missing entry point, or a real bug. Investigate it before adding a keep rule or an allowlist entry, and never add a suppression.

## Report (what you hand back)

Order every finding by tier, most severe first, and inside a tier by count. The tier is about what the finding can do in production, not which tool found it:

| Tier | What belongs in it | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **High** | can lose data, lose an error, crash, or run wrong in production; or no gate enforces anything | a swallowed or replaced exception, a silent fallback, an unsynchronized shared collection, a dereference of a value that can be `null` at a boundary, two versions of one library on the runtime classpath, gates not wired into CI |
| **Medium** | costs maintenance or resources, or will break on the next upgrade | duplication, complexity and size, mutable statics and `ThreadLocal`s, unclosed resources, dead code, JDK-internal APIs in dependencies, the test JVM outside its bounds, production JVM headroom |
| **Low** | says more than it does, or hides nothing yet | suppressions, test shape, unnecessary qualifiers, missing `@Override`, Javadoc tags, likely false positives of security detectors |

Every finding names file:line, the rule, and whether fixing it changes behaviour (rule 5). A finding you found by reading the code, with no gate behind it, says so, and says which gate would have caught it.

# Agent brief: set up and keep quality gates for dead code, duplication and "slop"

> **Proven on 2026-09-25** in a throwaway repo (Python 3.12 + TypeScript, macOS, Node 24) built only from this file: the pinned installs of Phase 1, every config and script copied as written, `scripts/validate.sh` green on clean code, all 20 planted violations of Phase 4 failing their gate, and both mutation paths reporting survivors (mutmut with `--patch`: 5 on a weakly tested function; Stryker with a `file:5-9` range: 3 of 4 mutants, all on those lines). The three gaps that run found are fixed below: a stale `noqa`, pyright unseen by knip, and the import roots of a source layout.

You are setting up a repository's quality gates from nothing, then fixing the code until every gate passes. After that, the gates keep the code in that shape. This file is self-contained: every config, script and helper you need is in it. Copy the blocks as written, change only the placeholders marked `<LIKE_THIS>`, and follow the phases in order.

**What "slop" means here**, and the gate that catches each kind:

| Slop | Caught by |
| --- | --- |
| A function, file, export, parameter or dependency nothing uses | vulture (Python), knip + `noUnused*` (TypeScript), ruff `ARG`/`F401` |
| Copy-pasted code, including a test that re-implements the code it tests | jscpd over code **and** tests in one run |
| An import that does not import (unused, or a re-export barrel) | ruff `F401`, tsc `noUnusedLocals`, knip, `no-re-exports` |
| Logic that says more than it does: a guard that can never fire, a cast to the type it already has, `if x: return True else: return False`, a loop that appends where a comprehension says it | ruff `SIM`/`RET`/`PIE`/`C4`/`PERF`/`FURB`, pyright `reportUnnecessary*`, typescript-eslint `no-unnecessary-*` |
| A type that lies (index reads assumed present, a parameter typed `str` whose body checks `isinstance(x, str)`) | `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `no-unnecessary-condition`, `reportUnnecessaryIsInstance` |
| A promise nobody awaits | `no-floating-promises`, `no-misused-promises` |
| A test that does not test: asserts nothing, is skipped or focused, or passes whatever the code does | vitest rules, `check_tests_assert.py`, mutation testing on the changed lines |
| A suppression that hides any of the above | `eslint-comments/no-use`, `RUF100`, `reportUnnecessaryTypeIgnoreComment` |

## Ground rules (read twice)

1. **Zero is the gate.** A gate passes only when it has zero findings. Do not write per-area "debt ceiling" scripts. If a tree cannot reach zero in this change, use the tool's own baseline (jscpd `--baseline` + `--fail-on-new-clones`, or one `# noqa: C901` on the def line of a function over the complexity limit) and never raise it.
2. **Never suppress.** No `// eslint-disable`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, blanket `# noqa`, `# type: ignore` or `# pyright: ignore`. No non-null assertion `!`, and no `as T` just to drop `undefined`. Fix the code, or make the type tell the truth. The config bans the suppressions, so don't try to get around the ban.
3. **Measure before you enable.** Run each new rule once as a warning, count its findings, and record the count. Turn it into an error in the same change that fixes them.
4. **Prove every gate looked.** A gate that scanned nothing also passes. For every gate, plant one violation, see the gate fail with the expected message, and revert it (Phase 4). Report the proof.
5. **Do not change behaviour.** This work changes structure, types and tests, not what the program does. If a fix would change behaviour, stop and report it instead. Do not delete a test to make a gate pass; fix the test.
6. **One phase per commit, with conventional messages** (`chore:`, `test:`, `docs:`). Commit only if the person who asked you allows it. Stage files by name, never `git add .`.
7. **Keep what the repo already enforces.** If a stricter existing rule conflicts with this brief, keep the stricter one. If the repo uses a different tool for the same job (flake8, black, pylint), ruff replaces flake8/isort/pylint-lite. Keep black (or `ruff format`) for formatting only.
8. **Say what you could not verify.** A green command is not proof unless you also proved it scanned something (rule 4).

Merge these tables into the existing file; keep its other tables. Replace `<PY_DIRS>` and `<PY_VERSION>` (for example `py312`).

```toml

target-version = "<PY_VERSION>"
line-length = 120
extend-exclude = [".venv", "node_modules", "dist", "build"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "F", "E", "W", "I", "B", "UP", "SIM", "RUF",   # correctness, imports (F401), modernisation, simplification
    "ARG",                                           # unused arguments (dead parameters)
    "RET", "PIE", "C4", "PERF", "PLW0108",           # returns, placeholders, comprehensions, loops, lambda wrappers
    "PLR1714", "PLR5501", "PLR1730",                 # `x == a or x == b`, `else: if`, hand-written min/max
    "FURB110", "FURB171", "FURB188",                 # `a if a else b`, `x in (y,)`, slice instead of removeprefix
    "ERA001",                                        # commented-out code
    "C901", "PLR0911", "PLR0912", "PLR0915",         # complexity, returns, branches, statements per function
    "S", "BLE001", "TRY002", "TRY300", "TRY301", "TRY400", "T20", "PT",
]
ignore = ["E501", "SIM108"]
# Framework callbacks that must accept an argument and usually ignore it go here, by name, and nowhere else.
dummy-variable-rgx = "^(_+|(_+[a-zA-Z0-9_]*[a-zA-Z0-9]+?)|context)$"

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 12

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-branches = 15
max-statements = 60
max-returns = 8

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Tests assert (S101) and hold fake secrets (S105/S106). Nothing else is exempt: an unused argument in a test is dead too.
"**/test_*.py" = ["S101", "S105", "S106"]
"**/conftest.py" = ["S101", "S105"]
"scripts/**" = ["T201"]     # scripts talk to a terminal

[tool.vulture]
paths = [<PY_DIRS as quoted, comma-separated strings>]
# vulture scores every unused function, class, attribute and variable at exactly 60 %; a higher floor cannot report a dead function.
min_confidence = 60
sort_by_size = true
# Only real entry points and named seams that production defines and only tests call, each with a comment.
ignore_names = []
# Do NOT list your own route/handler decorators here: they would hide every dead handler.

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
```

### 2.5 [ts] `eslint-rules/no-re-exports.mjs`

This rule makes a module export only what it declares: no barrels, no `export … from`, no re-exporting an imported name. A barrel hides which file a name lives in, and keeps a file nobody else imports out of knip's unused-files report.

```js
function findVariable(scope, name) {
  const found = scope.set.get(name);
  if (found) return found;
  return scope.upper ? findVariable(scope.upper, name) : undefined;
}

function isImported(context, node, identifier) {
  if (identifier?.type !== 'Identifier') return false;
  const variable = findVariable(context.sourceCode.getScope(node), identifier.name);
  return Boolean(variable?.defs.some((definition) => definition.type === 'ImportBinding'));
}

export default {
  meta: {
    type: 'problem',
    docs: { description: "Disallow re-exporting another module's names; import from the defining module" },
    messages: {
      reExportFrom: "Re-export from '{{source}}': import from the defining module where the name is used, and delete this line.",
      reExportImport: "'{{name}}' is imported, not declared here: its importers should import it from the defining module.",
    },
    schema: [],
  },
  create(context) {
    const reportFrom = (node) => context.report({ node, messageId: 'reExportFrom', data: { source: node.source.value } });
    return {
      ExportAllDeclaration: reportFrom,
      ExportNamedDeclaration(node) {
        if (node.source) {
          reportFrom(node);
          return;
        }
        for (const specifier of node.specifiers) {
          if (isImported(context, node, specifier.local)) {
            context.report({ node: specifier, messageId: 'reExportImport', data: { name: specifier.local.name } });
          }
        }
      },
      ExportDefaultDeclaration(node) {
        if (isImported(context, node, node.declaration)) {
          context.report({ node, messageId: 'reExportImport', data: { name: node.declaration.name } });
        }
      },
    };
  },
};
```

A library's public entry file (the `main`/`exports` of a published package) is the one place a re-export can be legitimate. List that one file in an `ignores` of the rule's block, with a comment saying why.

### 2.10 [ts] `<TS_SRC>/test/definedValue.ts` (spec helper)

With `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `rows[0]` is `T | undefined`. Specs narrow with this helper instead of `!`, a cast, or a conditional in the test body:

```ts
/** A spec read a value its fixture promised and found nothing there: the fixture, not the code under test, is wrong. */
class FixtureValueMissingError extends Error {
  constructor(what: string) {
    super(`The fixture has no ${what}`);
    this.name = 'FixtureValueMissingError';
  }
}

/** `definedValue(rows[0], 'the first row')`: the value a spec indexes out of its own fixture, or a throw. */
export function definedValue<T>(value: T | undefined, what: string): T {
  if (value === undefined) {
    throw new FixtureValueMissingError(what);
  }
  return value;
}
```

Keep the class unexported: knip fails an export that nothing imports.

### 3.1 [py] `scripts/lint-python.sh`: vulture in two passes

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dead Python code, two passes, one gate.
#   --dead-code        production code with the tests left out: a function only a test calls is dead.
#   --dead-code-tests  the whole tree, printing only what the first pass did not: dead test helpers and fixtures.
# Paths, floor and allowlists live in pyproject.toml [tool.vulture]; vulture's CLI flags REPLACE pyproject
# values, so this script passes only the excludes, which are the one thing the passes differ in.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.."

EXCLUDE='*/.venv/*,*/node_modules/*,*/__pycache__/*,*/dist/*,*/build/*'
TEST_FILES='*/test_*.py,*_test.py,*/conftest.py'
FOUND_EXIT=3

case "${1:-}" in
  --dead-code)
    vulture --exclude "$EXCLUDE,$TEST_FILES"
    ;;
  --dead-code-tests)
    production="$(vulture --exclude "$EXCLUDE,$TEST_FILES" || true)"
    everything="$(vulture --exclude "$EXCLUDE" || true)"
    if [[ -z "$production" ]]; then
      tests_only="$everything"
    else
      tests_only="$(grep -vxF -f <(printf '%s\n' "$production") <<<"$everything" || true)"
    fi
    if [[ -n "$tests_only" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$tests_only"
      exit "$FOUND_EXIT"
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    echo "usage: $0 --dead-code | --dead-code-tests" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac
```

### 3.2 [py] `scripts/check_tests_assert.py`: every pytest test asserts

ruff has no "test without an assertion" rule, so this small script adds one.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Every pytest test asserts something: a bare ``assert``, ``pytest.raises``/``warns``/``fail``, a mock's
``assert_*`` method, or a local helper that does one of those (followed through the module's own functions).
A test that asserts nothing passes whatever the code does. Exit 1 listing each one."""
from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import subprocess
import sys

ASSERTING_CALLS = {'raises', 'warns', 'fail', 'deprecated_call'}
ASSERTING_PREFIXES = ('assert', 'expect')


def _call_name(call: ast.Call) -> str:
    func = call.func
    if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute):
        return func.attr
    return func.id if isinstance(func, ast.Name) else ''


def _asserts(node: ast.AST, helpers: dict[str, ast.AST], seen: set[str]) -> bool:
    for sub in ast.walk(node):
        if isinstance(sub, ast.Assert):
            return True
        if not isinstance(sub, ast.Call):
            continue
        name = _call_name(sub)
        if name in ASSERTING_CALLS or name.startswith(ASSERTING_PREFIXES):
            return True
        if name in helpers and name not in seen:
            seen.add(name)
            if _asserts(helpers[name], helpers, seen):
                return True
    return False


def _test_files() -> list[str]:
    listed = subprocess.run(['git', 'ls-files', '*.py'], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.split()  # noqa: S607 — git from PATH
    return [f for f in listed if f.rsplit('/', 1)[-1].startswith('test_') or f.endswith('_test.py')]


def main() -> int:
    silent: list[str] = []
    for path in _test_files():
        with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as handle:
            tree = ast.parse(handle.read(), filename=path)
        functions = [n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)]
        helpers = {f.name: f for f in functions if not f.name.startswith('test_')}
        silent.extend(
            f'{path}:{f.lineno} {f.name}' for f in functions if f.name.startswith('test_') and not _asserts(f, helpers, set())
        )
    for line in silent:
        print(f'test asserts nothing: {line}')
    return 1 if silent else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())
```

A "does not raise" test still needs an assertion on its result (`assert fn(x) is None`). If you want this script's own behaviour pinned, give it a test.

### 3.3 [py] `scripts/mutate-python.sh`: mutation testing, whole module or changed lines

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Mutation testing for one Python module (mutmut 2.x). Not a gate: a per-module tool, run on what a change touches.
#
#   scripts/mutate-python.sh [--patch <git-range>] <module.py> <test file or dir> [more tests...]
#   scripts/mutate-python.sh --patch origin/main src/pricing.py tests/test_pricing.py
#
# --patch mutates only the lines the range added or changed in the module (`git diff <range>`; a single ref
# compares it with the working tree). A mutant the tests kill is behaviour they pin. A survivor is either a
# statement no test observes (strengthen the test) or a statement with no effect (delete it); an equivalent
# mutant is the one case to leave, marked `# pragma: no mutate` with the reason.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.."

PATCH_RANGE=""
if [[ "${1:-}" == "--patch" ]]; then
  PATCH_RANGE="${2:-}"
  shift 2 || true
fi
if [[ $# -lt 2 || "$PATCH_RANGE" == -* ]]; then
  sed -n '4,5p' "$0" >&2
  exit 2
fi
MODULE="$1"; shift
TESTS=("$@")
PYTHON="${PYTHON_BIN:-python}"

rm -f .mutmut-cache   # a clean cache per run: another module's entries only confuse `mutmut results`

PATCH_ARGS=()
if [[ -n "$PATCH_RANGE" ]]; then
  PATCH_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/mutmut-patch.XXXXXX")"
  trap 'rm -f "$PATCH_FILE"' EXIT
  git diff --unified=0 --no-ext-diff "$PATCH_RANGE" -- "$MODULE" > "$PATCH_FILE"
  if [[ ! -s "$PATCH_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "No lines of $MODULE changed in $PATCH_RANGE: nothing to mutate (drop --patch for the whole module)" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  PATCH_ARGS=(--use-patch-file "$PATCH_FILE")
fi

echo "==> Baseline: the tests must pass unmutated"
"$PYTHON" -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider "${TESTS[@]}"

echo "==> Mutating ${PATCH_RANGE:+the lines changed in $PATCH_RANGE of }$MODULE"
# mutmut 2 counts only exit 1 as "killed"; pytest exits 2 when a mutant breaks the import (a collection
# error), which would count as survived, hence `|| exit 1`. -x: one failing test is enough.
mutmut run \
  --paths-to-mutate "$MODULE" \
  --tests-dir "$(dirname "${TESTS[0]}")" \
  --runner "sh -c '$PYTHON -m pytest -x -q -p no:cacheprovider ${TESTS[*]} || exit 1'" \
  ${PATCH_ARGS[@]+"${PATCH_ARGS[@]}"} \
  --no-progress || true   # mutmut exits non-zero when mutants survive; the results below are the point

# An interrupted run can leave a mutant in the file; mutmut keeps the original in <module>.bak.
if [[ -f "$MODULE.bak" ]]; then mv -f "$MODULE.bak" "$MODULE"; fi

echo "==> Results (mutmut show <id> prints a survivor's diff)"
mutmut results || true
```

Do not run git commands that write to the tree (checkout, stash, commit) while a mutation run is going: mutmut rewrites the module in place.

### 3.4 `scripts/mutation-report.sh`: the release's changed lines, mutated against their tests

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The mutation report of a change: every module it touched, mutated against its own tests, only the
# lines it added or changed (a module whose test alone changed is mutated whole: a test change is the
# moment to ask what else the tests miss). A report you act on before merging/releasing, not a gate.
#
#   scripts/mutation-report.sh <base-ref>            # e.g. origin/main, or the last release tag
#   scripts/mutation-report.sh <base-ref> --whole    # every changed module whole
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.."
BASE="${1:?usage: $0 <base-ref> [--whole]}"
WHOLE="${2:-}"

own_lines_changed() { [[ "$WHOLE" != "--whole" ]] && ! git diff --quiet "$BASE" -- "$1"; }

# ---- Python: module -> its namesake test (test_<stem>.py anywhere in the repo) ----
py_changed() {
  git diff --name-only "$BASE" -- '*.py' | while IFS= read -r f; do
    base="$(basename "$f")"
    case "$base" in
      conftest.py|__init__.py) ;;
      test_*.py) stem="${base#test_}"; git ls-files "*/$stem" "$stem" | head -1 ;;
      *) [[ -f "$f" ]] && echo "$f" ;;
    esac
  done | sort -u
}
for module in $(py_changed); do
  stem="$(basename "$module" .py)"
  tests="$(git ls-files "*test_${stem//-/_}.py" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  if [[ -z "$tests" ]]; then echo "--- $module: NO TESTS (a finding)"; continue; fi
  scope=()
  own_lines_changed "$module" && scope=(--patch "$BASE")
  echo "--- $module (${scope[*]:-whole}) against: $tests"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  bash scripts/mutate-python.sh ${scope[@]+"${scope[@]}"} "$module" $tests || echo "    (tests fail unmutated, or no changed lines)"
done

# ---- TypeScript: file -> its spec beside it; Stryker line ranges per changed hunk ----
# Set PKG to the package directory that holds stryker.config.mjs (e.g. "web"), or "." for the root.
PKG="${PKG:-.}"
ts_changed() {
  git diff --name-only "$BASE" -- "$PKG" | grep -E '\.tsx?$' | grep -vE '\.d\.ts$|-fixtures\.|/test/' | while IFS= read -r f; do
    case "$f" in
      *.spec.ts|*.spec.tsx|*.test.ts|*.test.tsx) m="$(sed -E 's/\.(spec|test)\.(tsx?)$/.\2/' <<<"$f")"; [[ -f "$m" ]] && echo "$m" ;;
      *) [[ -f "$f" ]] && echo "$f" ;;
    esac
  done | sort -u
}
for file in $(ts_changed); do
  ext="${file##*.}"; spec_a="${file%.*}.spec.$ext"; spec_b="${file%.*}.test.$ext"
  if [[ ! -f "$spec_a" && ! -f "$spec_b" ]]; then echo "--- $file: NO SPEC (a finding)"; continue; fi
  relative="${file#"$PKG"/}"
  target="$relative"
  if own_lines_changed "$file"; then
    target="$(git diff --unified=0 "$BASE" -- "$file" \
      | sed -nE 's/^@@ -[0-9,]+ \+([0-9]+)(,([0-9]+))? @@.*/\1 \3/p' \
      | awk -v f="$relative" '{ n = ($2 == "" ? 1 : $2); if (n > 0) printf "%s%s:%d-%d", (c++ ? "," : ""), f, $1, $1 + n - 1 }')"
  fi
  if [[ -z "$target" ]]; then echo "--- $file: only deletions"; continue; fi
  echo "--- $file ($target)"
  (cd "$PKG" && npx stryker run --mutate "$target") | grep -E '^\[Survived\]|^[-+] |^ *[A-Za-z].*\|' || true
done
```

Every survivor the report prints gets exactly one outcome before merge or release:
- a test that kills it;
- deleting the statement it proves has no effect;
- an equivalence marker with its reason (`# pragma: no mutate`, or `// Stryker disable next-line <mutator>: <reason>`).

### 3.5 `scripts/validate.sh`: every gate, in order, each a hard stop

Delete the steps for a language the repo does not have. Add one `tsc` step per TypeScript program and one knip/vitest pair per JS/TS package. CI runs this script and nothing else.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.."
# One command per step: under `set -e` a failure on the left of `&&` does not stop the script.

if [[ -z "${PYTHON_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  if [[ -x .venv/bin/python ]]; then PYTHON_BIN="$PWD/.venv/bin/python"; else PYTHON_BIN="$(command -v python3)"; fi
fi
export PYTHON_BIN
PATH="$(dirname "$PYTHON_BIN"):$PATH"   # ruff, vulture, pytest from the same environment
export PATH
step() { printf '\n==> %s\n' "$1"; }

# ---- Python ----
step "ruff";                              ruff check <PY_DIRS>
step "vulture: production code";          bash scripts/lint-python.sh --dead-code
step "vulture: test-support code";        bash scripts/lint-python.sh --dead-code-tests
step "pyright";                           npx pyright --pythonpath "$PYTHON_BIN"
step "every test asserts";                "$PYTHON_BIN" scripts/check_tests_assert.py
step "pytest";                            "$PYTHON_BIN" -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider

# ---- TypeScript (repeat per program / package) ----
step "tsc: <program>";                    npx tsc -p <tsconfig.json> --noEmit
step "eslint";                            npx eslint .
step "knip: <pkg>";                       (cd <pkg> && npx knip)
step "knip --production: <pkg>";          (cd <pkg> && npx knip --config <rel-path-to>/scripts/knip-production.mjs --production --strict)
step "vitest: <pkg>";                     (cd <pkg> && npx vitest run)

# ---- Everything ----
step "jscpd: code and tests";             npx jscpd --fail-on-empty

printf '\nvalidate: every gate passed\n'
```

```json
  "duplication": "jscpd --fail-on-empty",
```

## Phase 5: baseline, then fix, in this order

Run every new rule once as a warning, count the findings (commands below), and write the counts down. Then fix one group, turn it on as an error, run `scripts/validate.sh`, and commit. The order goes from the cheapest group to the most invasive.

```bash
# counts, before enabling (Python)
ruff check <PY_DIRS> --statistics --select PIE,C4,PERF,RET,PLW0108,PLR1714,PLR5501,PLR1730,FURB110,FURB171,FURB188,ARG
# counts, before enabling (TS): run eslint once with the new rules at "warn" and count per rule
npx eslint . -f json -o /tmp/eslint.json; node -e 'const r=require("/tmp/eslint.json");const c={};for(const f of r)for(const m of f.messages)c[m.ruleId]=(c[m.ruleId]||0)+1;console.log(c)'
# counts, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, per program
npx tsc -p <tsconfig.json> --noEmit --noUncheckedIndexedAccess 2>&1 | grep -c 'error TS'
```

1. **Dead code, imports and duplication**: vulture, knip, `F401`/`ARG`, `no-re-exports`, jscpd. Delete what is dead. Wire in what is really used but invisible to the tool (an entry point, a CLI named only in a config file), and add a comment saying why. Extract duplicates into a module with a specific name, never `utils`. Put shared spec data in `*-fixtures.ts` or `conftest.py`.
2. **Logic that says more than it does**: ruff `PIE C4 PERF RET PLW0108 PLR… FURB…`, pyright `reportUnnecessary*`, typescript-eslint `no-unnecessary-type-assertion`, `boolean-literal-compare`, `template-expression`, `redundant-type-constituents`, `no-else-return`, `no-lonely-if`, the unicorn rules. `ruff check --fix` and `eslint --fix` do most of it. Review every automatic change, especially `--unsafe-fixes`.
3. **Tests that test**: `vitest/*`, `check_tests_assert.py`. Rename assertion helpers to `expect…`. Fill in or delete empty tests; a test named "never raises" asserts on the result.
4. **Types that do not lie**: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` in every tsconfig, then `no-unnecessary-condition`, `no-floating-promises`, `no-misused-promises`. This is the largest group. If it has more than about 150 findings, split the tree into folders that do not overlap and give each worker the "how to fix" rules below. Afterwards, re-run jscpd (new `definedValue(...)` lines can create clones) and knip (removing a `?? x.field` read can leave a type member unread).
5. **Mutation on the change**: run `scripts/mutation-report.sh <base>` on the branch. Kill, delete or mark every survivor.

### How to fix each kind (the rules that keep the fix from becoming new slop)

- **An index read in production code**: prefer a shape that is provably safe:
  - destructuring with a default (`const [first = fallback] = list`);
  - `.find(...)`, `for (const x of list)` or `Object.entries(...)`;
  - a `Map` instead of an object used as a map;
  - a non-empty tuple type (`readonly [T, ...T[]]`) for a list that is fixed by design.

  Use `?? fallback` only when the fallback is what the code *should* do. If absence is impossible and nothing sensible can replace it, throw a small named error class. Never use `!`, and never cast.
- **An index read in a spec**: `definedValue(rows[0], 'the first row')`, or assert the whole structure with `toStrictEqual([...])`.
- **A guard the types say can never fire** (`no-unnecessary-condition`, `reportUnnecessaryIsInstance`), first decide where the value comes from:
  - **It crosses a boundary** (HTTP body, `JSON.parse`, model output, `localStorage`, env var, DOM): keep the guard and make the type honest. Mark the field optional, type the parameter `object`/`unknown`/`list[Any]`, or read it through a local `Partial<…>`.
  - **It is internal and already has that type**: delete the guard.
  - **Check the producer (the backend, the parser) before deciding.** If a shared type lies about a response, fix the type at its source rather than per consumer, and list any you leave.
- **A floating promise**:
  - `await` it when order matters.
  - `void p` only when `p` already catches its own errors (check it).
  - Otherwise add a `.catch(...)` that does what the surrounding code does with errors.
  - In specs, `await` it.
- **A dead parameter** (`ARG`): remove it from the signature and every caller. If a framework requires it, name it `_name`, or add its name to `dummy-variable-rgx` once for the whole repo.
- **Complexity over 12**: extract a pure helper or a sibling component. Do not raise the limit.
- **A test the new rules flag**: fix the test's shape (split it at 4 `expect`s, move a conditional into a helper that throws). Never delete an assertion to pass `max-expects`: move it into its own test.

## Phase 6: keep it (every future change)

- Run `scripts/validate.sh` before calling any change done. Green means every gate, not "mostly".
- Before merging or releasing, run `scripts/mutation-report.sh <base-ref>` and resolve every survivor it names (kill, delete, or mark as equivalent with a reason). Write the survivor count and what you did about each into the PR or release notes.
- Adding code:
  - Export only what another module imports.
  - A function or export only a test uses is dead.
  - A new cross-language copy of a constant needs a test that reads both copies.
  - New spec helpers go in `*-fixtures.ts`, `src/test/` or `conftest.py`.
  - No new `jscpd:ignore` without its reason; no new entry in any allowlist without its comment.
- Never raise a limit (complexity 12, depth 3, 400 lines, 4 expects, 0 clones, 60 % vulture). If something cannot fit, split it.
- A finding that looks wrong is usually a type that lies, a missing entry point, or a real bug. Investigate it before adding an allowlist entry, and never add a suppression comment.

You are setting up a repository's quality gates from nothing, then fixing the code until every gate passes.
After that, the gates keep the code in that shape. This file is self-contained: every config, script and rule
you need is in it. Copy the blocks as written, change only the placeholders marked `<LIKE_THIS>`, and follow
the phases in order.

**What "slop" means here**, and the gate that catches each kind:

| Slop | Rust | TypeScript |
| --- | --- | --- |

## Ground rules (read twice)

1. **Zero is the gate.** A gate passes only with zero findings. No per-area "debt ceiling" scripts. If a tree
   cannot reach zero in this change, use the tool's own baseline (jscpd `--baseline` + `--fail-on-new-clones`)
   and never raise it.
2. **Never suppress.** No `#[allow(..)]`, `#[expect(..)]`, `#![allow(..)]`, `#[cfg_attr(.., allow(..))]`,
   `// eslint-disable`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, non-null `!`, `as T` to drop `undefined`, or
   `.unwrap()` to make a type checker quiet. Fix the code, or make the type tell the truth. The only exceptions
   live in config files (`Cargo.toml` lint table, `clippy.toml`, `deny.toml`, an ast-grep rule's `ignores:`),
   each with a comment saying why.
3. **Measure before you enable.** Run each new rule once as a warning, count its findings, and record the count.
   Turn it into an error in the same change that fixes them.
4. **Prove every gate looked.** A gate that scanned nothing also passes. For every gate, plant one violation,
   see it fail with the expected message, and revert it (Phase 4).
5. **Do not change behaviour.** This work changes structure, types and tests, not what the program does. If a
   fix would change behaviour (for example, replacing a panic with an error the caller now has to handle),
   stop and report it. Do not delete a test to make a gate pass; fix the test.
6. **One phase per commit, with conventional messages** (`chore:`, `test:`, `docs:`). Commit only if the person
   who asked you allows it. Stage files by name, never `git add .`.
7. **Keep what the repo already enforces.** If a stricter existing rule conflicts with this brief, keep the
   stricter one. Merge into existing `clippy.toml`, `deny.toml`, `rustfmt.toml` and ESLint configs.
8. **Say what you could not verify.** A green command is not proof unless you also proved it scanned something.

### 2.1 [rust] `rust-toolchain.toml` (in each `<RUST_DIR>`)

```toml
# The compiler, clippy and rustfmt every gate runs with. Bump it in its own change and rerun Phase 4:
# a new clippy can add findings to lints that are already on.
[toolchain]
channel = "<1.99.1>"
components = ["clippy", "rustfmt"]
profile = "minimal"
```

Trap [checked]: any `cargo`/`rustup` command in a directory with this file installs the pinned toolchain if it
is missing (463 MB). In scratch copies where you do not want that, set `RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL=0`. [proven 2026-11-11]
A `stable` toolchain that is the same version does not count: rustup installs `1.99.1-<host>` beside it.
The pinned toolchain has only the targets the file lists: add `targets = ["wasm32-unknown-unknown", …]` for every
target a build or a clippy step uses (web, Lambda cross-builds), or those builds fail on a machine that had the
targets under `stable` [docs]. The pin also governs the release builds, so in a repo that deploys from another
machine it is agreed with whoever deploys.

### 2.2 [rust] lints in the workspace `Cargo.toml`

Every lint is `warn`; `scripts/validate.sh` runs clippy with `-D warnings`, which turns every warning (rustc's
and clippy's) into an error [checked]. Warn, not deny, so a developer's `cargo build` and `cargo test` still run
while code is half written. Groups first (`priority = -1`), then single lints, which override their group.
Every member crate gets `[lints] workspace = true`. A crate that must write `unsafe` cannot override one lint of
an inherited table (Cargo does not merge them): give it a copy of this table with `unsafe_code` removed, and say
why in a comment.

```toml

rust_2018_idioms = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }  # elided_lifetimes_in_paths, bare_trait_objects, ...
unreachable_pub = "warn"          # `pub` on an item nothing outside the crate can reach: say pub(crate), and dead_code sees it
```


Trap [checked]: clippy does not notice a newly created `clippy.toml` until a source file of the crate changes
(edits to an existing one are picked up). After creating it, `touch` one source file per crate before measuring.

Rust has no cyclomatic-complexity lint; `cognitive_complexity` is off on purpose (clippy moved it out of the
default groups because its scores are not reliable). `too_many_lines` and `excessive_nesting` are the limits.

### 2.5 [rust] ast-grep rules: what rustc and clippy do not check

At the repo root: `sgconfig.yml`, `sg/utils/*.yml`, `sg/rules/*.yml`, `sg/rule-tests/*.yml`. ast-grep parses
Rust with tree-sitter; attributes such as `#[test]` are the function's preceding **siblings**, not its children,
which is why the rules use `follows`. [proven 2026-11-11: `ast-grep test` passes every case as written, each
rule fails on its plant (Phase 4), and the scan of 1839 Rust files of a real repo gave 251 suppressions, 11 ignored
tests, 7 tests asserting nothing, and 21 commented-out-code hits that were all prose (fixed below).]

Vendored code that must stay as its upstream wrote it (and checked-in generated files) goes in each rule's
`ignores:`, with the reason [fixed 2026-11-11: the rules had no place for it]:

```yaml
ignores:
  # vendored upstream code: pristine by design; our overlay is outside it
  - "**/upstream/**"
```

`sgconfig.yml`:

```yaml
# ast-grep 0.51.1: the Rust source checks clippy and rustc do not provide. `npx ast-grep scan` runs every rule;
# `npx ast-grep test` runs the fixtures in sg/rule-tests.
ruleDirs: [sg/rules]
utilDirs: [sg/utils]
testConfigs:
  - testDir: sg/rule-tests
```

`sg/utils/rust-test-fn.yml`:

```yaml
# A function with a test attribute. Attributes are the fn's preceding SIBLINGS, so this walks back over
# attributes and comments and stops at the first other node.
id: rust-test-fn
language: Rust
rule:
  kind: function_item
  follows:
    stopBy:
      not:
        any: [{ kind: attribute_item }, { kind: line_comment }, { kind: block_comment }]
    kind: attribute_item
    # test, tokio::test, test_log::test, sqlx::test, rstest, test_case, wasm_bindgen_test
    regex: '^#\[\s*(?:[A-Za-z_]\w*\s*::\s*)*(?:test|rstest|test_case|wasm_bindgen_test)\b'
```

`sg/utils/rust-direct-assertion.yml`:

```yaml
# An assertion written in place: an assert-family macro, panic!/unreachable!, or a call to a function, method or
# macro named assert_*/expect_* (helpers, mock expectations, assert_cmd's `.assert()`).
# `.unwrap()`, `.expect(..)` and `?` are not assertions: they only say "no error".
id: rust-direct-assertion
language: Rust
rule:
  any:
    - kind: macro_invocation
      has:
        field: macro
        regex: '(?:^|::)(?:assert\w*|debug_assert\w*|prop_assert\w*|expect_\w*|panic|unreachable)$'
    - kind: call_expression
      has:
        field: function
        regex: '(?:^|[.:])(?:assert(?:_\w*)?|expect_\w*)(?:::<.*>)?$'
```

`sg/utils/rust-assertion.yml`:

```yaml
# An assertion: in place, or a call to a function or macro_rules! macro of the same file whose body asserts in
# place (one level, like a helper you can read on the same screen).
id: rust-assertion
language: Rust
rule:
  any:
    - matches: rust-direct-assertion
    - kind: call_expression
      all:
        - has:
            field: function
            any:
              - { kind: identifier, pattern: $HELPER }
              - { kind: scoped_identifier, has: { field: name, pattern: $HELPER } }
        - inside:
            kind: source_file
            stopBy: end
            has:
              stopBy: end
              kind: function_item
              all:
                - has: { field: name, pattern: $HELPER }
                - has: { stopBy: end, matches: rust-direct-assertion }
    - kind: macro_invocation
      all:
        - has: { field: macro, pattern: $MACRO }
        - inside:
            kind: source_file
            stopBy: end
            has:
              stopBy: end
              kind: macro_definition
              all:
                - has: { field: name, pattern: $MACRO }
                - regex: '(?:assert\w*|debug_assert\w*|prop_assert\w*|panic|unreachable)\s*!'
```

`sg/rules/rust-test-asserts-nothing.yml`:

```yaml
id: rust-test-asserts-nothing
language: Rust
severity: error
message: test asserts nothing
note: >-
  A test that calls code and asserts nothing passes whatever the code does. Assert on the result
  (`?`, `.unwrap()` and `.expect()` alone only say "no error"), use #[should_panic(expected = "...")],
  or call a helper named assert_*/expect_* that asserts.
rule:
  matches: rust-test-fn
  not:
    any:
      - follows:
          stopBy:
            not:
              any: [{ kind: attribute_item }, { kind: line_comment }, { kind: block_comment }]
          kind: attribute_item
          regex: '^#\[\s*should_panic\b'
      - has: { stopBy: end, matches: rust-assertion }
```

`sg/rules/rust-assert-helper-asserts-nothing.yml`:

```yaml
id: rust-assert-helper-asserts-nothing
language: Rust
severity: error
message: helper named like an assertion asserts nothing
note: >-
  A test that calls an assert_*/expect_* function or macro counts as asserting, so the helper must assert:
  an assert-family macro, panic!, or another assert_*/expect_* call.
rule:
  any:
    - kind: function_item
      has: { field: name, regex: '^(?:assert|expect)_' }
      not: { has: { stopBy: end, matches: rust-direct-assertion } }
    - kind: macro_definition
      has: { field: name, regex: '^(?:assert|expect)_' }
      not:
        regex: '(?:assert\w*|debug_assert\w*|prop_assert\w*|expect_\w*|panic|unreachable)\s*!|(?:assert|expect)_\w*\s*\('
```

`sg/rules/rust-no-lint-suppression.yml`:

```yaml
id: rust-no-lint-suppression
language: Rust
severity: error
message: lint suppression attribute
note: >-
  Fix the finding instead of silencing it (#[allow], #[expect], #![allow], #![expect], or either one inside
  #[cfg_attr(..)]). clippy::allow_attributes only covers #[allow]. An exception is a file in this rule's
  `ignores:` list, with a comment saying why.
# ignores:
#   - "<path/to/generated.rs>"   # <why: generated by build.rs from <schema>; never edited by hand>
rule:
  any:
    - kind: attribute_item
    - kind: inner_attribute_item
  regex: '^#!?\[\s*(?:allow|expect)\s*\(|^#!?\[\s*cfg_attr\s*\((?s:.*)\b(?:allow|expect)\s*\('
```

`sg/rules/rust-no-ignored-test.yml`:

```yaml
id: rust-no-ignored-test
language: Rust
severity: error
message: disabled test
note: >-
  An ignored test passes whatever the code does. Make it run (fast, hermetic) or delete it; a reason string
  does not change that. cfg(any()) is always false and disables an item the same way.
rule:
  kind: attribute_item
  regex: '^#\[\s*ignore\b|^#\[\s*cfg_attr\s*\((?s:.*)\bignore\b|^#\[\s*cfg\s*\(\s*any\s*\(\s*\)\s*\)'
```

`sg/rules/rust-no-commented-out-code.yml` (a heuristic like ruff's ERA001; measure it in Phase 5 and tighten a
regex that hits prose, never add an ignore):

```yaml
id: rust-no-commented-out-code
language: Rust
severity: error
message: commented-out code
note: >-
  Delete it; git keeps the history. Doc comments (/// //! /** /*!) and their doctests are not checked. Prose
  that starts like code (`// if the cache is cold, ...`) does not match: only a line shaped like Rust does
  (`let x = ..`, `fn f(`, `use a::b;`, `if .. {`, `x = ..;`, `f(..);`, `a.b(..);`, a lone `}`).
rule:
  any:
    - kind: line_comment
      not: { regex: '^//(?:!|/(?:[^/]|$))' }          # /// and //! are docs
      any:
        - regex: '^//\s*(?:let\s+(?:mut\s+)?[A-Za-z_(][\w, ()]*\s*(?::[^=]*)?=[^=>]|(?:pub(?:\([\w:]+\))?\s+)?(?:async\s+|const\s+|unsafe\s+)*fn\s+\w+\s*[<(])'
        - regex: '^//\s*(?:pub(?:\([\w:]+\))?\s+)?(?:use\s+[\w:{}*, ]+;|mod\s+\w+\s*[;{]|(?:struct|enum|trait|union)\s+\w+.*[{;(]\s*$|impl\b.*\{\s*$|type\s+\w+.*=.*;\s*$)'
        - regex: '^//\s*(?:\}\s*else\s*(?:if\b.*)?\{\s*$|(?:if|while|match)\s+.+\{\s*$|for\s+.+\s+in\s+.+\{\s*$|loop\s*\{\s*$|return\b.*;\s*$|else\s*\{\s*$)'
        # a statement: an assignment, or a call/macro/method chain, then `;` (prose that ends in `;` does not match)
        - regex: '^//\s*(?:break|continue|[\w.:\[\]&*]+\s*[-+*/|&^]?=\s*[^=\s].*|[\w:.]+!?\(.*\)[\w.()?:<>]*)\s*;\s*$'
        - regex: '^//\s*[})\]]+\s*[;,)]*\s*$'          # a lone closing brace or bracket
        - regex: '^//\s*#!?\[\w'                       # an attribute
    - kind: block_comment
      not: { regex: '^/\*(?:!|\*(?:[^*/]|$))' }        # /** and /*! are docs
      regex: '(?m)^\s*(?:/\*+|\*+)?\s*(?:let\s+(?:mut\s+)?\w+\s*(?::[^=]*)?=[^=>]|(?:pub\s+)?fn\s+\w+\s*[<(]|use\s+[\w:{}*, ]+;|(?:if|while|match|for)\s+.+\{\s*$|(?:break|continue|[\w.:\[\]&*]+\s*[-+*/|&^]?=\s*[^=\s].*|[\w:.]+!?\(.*\)[\w.()?:<>]*)\s*;\s*(?:\*/)?\s*$|[})\]]+\s*[;,]?\s*(?:\*/)?\s*$)'
```

[fixed 2026-11-11] The statement arm was `'^//.*\S;\s*$'` (any comment ending in `;`). On a real repo whose prose
uses semicolons, all 21 hits were sentences (`// … reading only what the page already shows;`) and none was code.
It now needs a statement's shape; the fixtures below hold both sides.

### 2.6 [rust] `.cargo/mutants.toml` (in `<RUST_DIR>`)

```toml
# cargo-mutants 27.1.0. List values here are appended to the command line's; scalars on the command line win.
# Each exclusion names ONE equivalent mutant, as `cargo mutants --list` prints it ("path:line:col: name"),
# with the reason on the line above. An exclusion that names a whole file or function is not allowed.
exclude_re = [
    # '<why the mutant cannot change behaviour>'
    # '^crates/<crate>/src/<file>\.rs:\d+:\d+: replace > with >= in <fn>$',
]
# Mutants build and test with the committed lockfile, like CI.
additional_cargo_args = ["--locked"]
# cargo test, not nextest: nextest skips doctests, so behaviour only a doctest checks would show as MISSED.
test_tool = "cargo"
# Under the gitignored target/, never in the source tree.
output = "target/mutants"
```

[checked] `exclude_re` matches the `path:line:col: name` text; `#[mutants::skip]` needs the `mutants` crate as a
dependency (`#[cfg_attr(test, mutants::skip)]` with `mutants = "0.0.4"` as a dev-dependency works; `any()`,
`not(test)` forms are not honoured). Prefer the config entry: it keeps the reason next to it and no attribute
in the source.

[proven 2026-11-11] Two traps. An agent sandbox may treat `.cargo/` as a protected path and refuse to write the file:
`cargo mutants --config <path/to/mutants.toml>` reads the same file from anywhere (its `--locked` was seen applied).
A repo whose policy forbids a `target/` in the tree (one shared target for the machine) passes `--output <dir outside
the tree>` and points `TMPDIR` at a big volume: each scratch copy builds in its own `target/` inside the copy.

### 2.7 [security] `deny.toml` (in `<RUST_DIR>`)

```toml

# An exception lives here with its reason, never in a CLI flag.

[graph]
# Check what any feature can pull in, not only the default build.
all-features = true
# Every platform by default. To check only what you ship, list the targets:
# targets = ["x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "aarch64-apple-darwin", "wasm32-unknown-unknown"]

[advisories]
```
